headline: 2026 US labor market 'not collapsing': slower payrolls, 4.2% unemployment, wage growth contained
summary: J.P. Morgan Private Bank's Senior Markets Economist characterized the 2026 US labor market as 'moderating, not collapsing,' with hiring trends stable and wage growth contained. June's 57,000 payroll gain was below expectations, and the unemployment rate held at 4.2%, but the broader picture suggests a soft-landing trajectory rather than recession.
key_facts: July jobs data (Aug 7) will test this thesis
